problem: "The input gate then adds it ⊙ c̃t" — the word "it" reads as ordinary English and hides the symbol. A student cannot tell whether "it" means i_t, f_t or c_t.
fix: "The input gate then adds i_t ⊙ c̃t, giving c_t = f_t ⊙ c_{t-1} + i_t ⊙ c̃t = 0.4 + i_t ⊙ c̃t."

problem: The convention h_t = (1 - z_t) ⊙ h_{t-1} + z_t ⊙ h̃_t is one of two common ones; several textbooks write h_t = z_t ⊙ h_{t-1} + (1 - z_t) ⊙ h̃_t, so the update gate there does the opposite job. Nothing in the text warns the student, and the quiz answer depends on the chapter's choice.
fix: Add one sentence: "Some books reverse the role of z_t and write h_t = z_t ⊙ h_{t-1} + (1 - z_t) ⊙ h̃_t; check which convention your paper uses before substituting numbers."

problem: The gate matrices are not given shapes. The text defines k and d in Section 1 but never says W_f, W_i, W_c, W_o are k × (k + d) and b_f, b_i, b_c, b_o are k-vectors, so the concatenation [h_{t-1}, x_t] has no stated length.
fix: "Each W is a k × (k + d) matrix and each b is a k-vector, because [h_{t-1}, x_t] has length k + d; all states c_t and h_t are k-vectors."

problem: Cross-references are written as plain text ("see Unit 2 for tags and CRF training", "The encoder side of 6.3") while the book format expects chapter links, so a phone reader cannot tap through.
fix: Turn both into links, e.g. tag sets and CRF training and 6.3, with the real chapter ids.
